To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the collection and circulation of personal data is a central element of contemporary capitalism and that this data is a form of capital.

data is now a form of capital, that data is accumulated and extracted in a way that resembles the extraction of natural resources, and that data is extracted from individuals and communities in ways that are not always consensual and often not compensatory.

(a) data is capital, (b) data is a distinct type of capital that is different from, yet rooted in, economic capital, and (c) data is a form of capital because of the perpetual accumulation cycle that drives it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how data has become a new form of capital in contemporary capitalism, and how this new form of capital is driving a new regime of datafication.
the ways in which the datafication of social life is transforming the economy and society.
how datafication is a form of capitalist accumulation, and what this means for the political economy of data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the collection of data, the extraction of value from data, and the use of this value to accumulate further capital is now a core part of contemporary capitalism.
datafication is an economic regime that has emerged as a response to the need for accumulation and the need to maintain a competitive position in the market.
datafication as an accumulation strategy is a form of extraction.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have argued that datafication is a political economic regime that is distinct from other forms of capitalism, but is rooted in the logic of accumulation.
the datafication of society is driven by the accumulation and extraction of data as capital, and that datafication is a form of capitalism that is distinct from economic capital.
the datafication of the economy is a form of capitalist accumulation, and that this process of accumulation is increasingly driven by the extraction of data.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we need to develop a more nuanced understanding of how data is extracted from people, places, and systems in order to better understand how datafication is changing the ways we work, live, and relate to one another.
the current datafication regime is not a neutral, technical process, but a political and economic one.
we need to be much more critical of datafication, and the ways in which it is used to extract value from data subjects.
